title: Army Abruptly Removes V Corps Commander from Poland-Based NATO Eastern Flank Post
detail: The Army relieved Lt. Gen. Charles Costanza from command of V Corps — the forward-deployed headquarters in Poland responsible for NATO eastern-flank operations and coordinating US support to Ukraine — on August 7, 2026, roughly two months before his planned departure. An Army spokesperson said only that 'the matter has been referred to the appropriate authority in accordance with Army regulations,' without disclosing a reason. Brig. Gen. John Mountford, V Corps' deputy commander, is serving as acting commander; Maj. Gen. Thomas Feltey, already Senate-confirmed as Costanza's successor, had been due to take over in October. The removal lands amid a broader shake-up of senior military ranks under Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, though a source familiar with the matter said Costanza's case is unrelated to that campaign.

title: US Intelligence: Putin Could Test NATO With Limited Strike on Member State by 2029
detail: US intelligence assessments reported August 7, 2026 indicate Russian President Putin could authorize a narrowly scoped attack on a NATO member — most likely the Baltic states or Poland — sometime between fall 2026 and 2029, aimed at fracturing alliance unity by testing Article 5 rather than pursuing full territorial conquest. The finding overturns a long-standing Washington assumption that Moscow would avoid direct confrontation with NATO while its forces remain committed in Ukraine, reflecting what officials describe as a shift in Putin's risk calculus. Possible forms range from cyberattacks to small-scale incursions; analysts cited a May 2026 drone strike on a Romanian apartment building and late-July cruise missile debris landing in Poland as prior probing incidents. A NATO land incursion is still rated unlikely but would trigger Article 5; the harder question, per analysts, is how the alliance would respond to sub-threshold cyber or hybrid provocations — precisely the credibility gap central to this tracker's Article 5 reliability theme.

media.caption: US intel warns Russia could launch limited attack on NATO ally in effort to fragment organization
